description: Retrieve readable OCR DjVuTXT or plain text from an Internet Archive item, including public-domain books, documents, scanned periodicals, and transcripts. Set max_chars for page size, then pass next_continuation as continuation with the same identifier and omit char_offset. Direct char_offset access remains available. To confirm a text file exists, call ia_get_item with format "DjVuTXT".

char_offset.description: Character offset to start reading from (default 0). For sequential pages use next_continuation as continuation instead. Omit char_offset when using continuation.

continuation.description: Opaque next_continuation from the previous page. Omit char_offset when using it; blank is omitted.

identifier.description: Internet Archive item identifier, e.g. "prideprejudice00aust" (Pride and Prejudice). Obtain from ia_search_items results.

max_chars.description: Maximum number of characters to return in this response. Defaults to the server-configured maximum (IA_MAX_SNAPSHOT_CHARS, typically 50 000); a larger value is served at that maximum, with a notice. Lower values reduce token usage.

name: ia_get_text

char_offset.description: Character offset used for this response.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_continuation`: A continuation is unknown, expired, belongs to another item, or its file changed. `range_unavailable`: The download ignored or returned an invalid conditional byte range. `ambiguous_pagination`: Both a nonblank continuation and char_offset were supplied. `item_not_found`: The identifier does not exist in the Internet Archive. `no_text_file`: The item exists but contains no readable text file (DjVuTXT or plain-text). `download_forbidden`: Access to this item is restricted — it is in a login-required or limited collection. `archive_unavailable`: The Internet Archive Metadata API or the text file download did not answer within the request timeout, could not be reached, answered HTTP 5xx after retries, 429, or another 4xx, or the metadata response was unreadable. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

has_more.description: True when there is more text beyond this slice. Use next_continuation, or add max_chars to char_offset if no token is available.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters this response could hold — the requested max_chars, or the server maximum when the request exceeded it.

next_continuation.description: Opaque next-page token; use as continuation with the same identifier and omit char_offset. Expires after one hour.

notice.description: Explains a max_chars clamp or why efficient continuation is unavailable, with the next char_offset or end-of-document status.

source_file.description: Filename of the source text file fetched from the item.

source_file_bytes.description: Size of the source text file in bytes, from the item manifest — a byte count, not a character count (non-ASCII text takes several bytes per character). Omitted when the manifest lists no size.

text.description: The text slice starting at char_offset up to max_chars characters.

title: Get Internet Archive Item Text
